- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1-2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price spike is followed by model overshoot, cap next period’s forecast at 10% below peak.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature reversal.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with recent underperformance.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) and forecast is erratic, smooth out 3–5 day moving average before forecasting.
